reviewed_regions.detail: BackingList::emplace_back constructs an ordinary complete Backing with new before append. erase unlinks then delete; list destruction deletes only Backing metadata. Links are ordinary typed pointers. There is no pointer tagging, offset arithmetic, type punning or dependency on later implicit-lifetime language rules.

Container owns complete Backing objects and is noncopyable/nonmovable. Iterator holds only Backing*. append, unlink, splice_one and splice_all never relocate an object. Both runtime creation sites use emplace_back and last; the former external list node and self-iterator are removed.

append sets previous to old tail and next to null, reconnects tail or initializes head. unlink fixes both neighbor directions and both endpoint cases, then clears removed links. splice_all joins ordered chains, fixes new boundary and clears source head/tail; empty source and self-splice return. All mutation sites serialize through domain mutex or an exclusively owned detached local list.

Node allocation/construction completes before existing links change. AllocationTable insertion failure erases the newly appended Backing before rethrow. Claim reservation/claim failure erases owner placeholder then the new Backing. No budget/provider admission occurs until these stages succeed. A new scalar-allocation fault seam has not been executed by this review.

Pending owner and Backing remain in domain list before unlock. Pending counter prevents quiet reset/trim/collect. During concurrent inserts/deletes the Backing pointer stays stable. After relock owner publication re-finds by exact ID; no Allocation slot pointer is carried across callback.

Valid owner or final lease under domain mutex identifies the sole Backing. Its owner record is consumed, then splice_one removes node from domain list before callback unlock. Detached local list owns node until callback and accounting reconciliation finish, including failure. No empty-list sentinel allocation or lookup scan occurs.

Quiet-only reclaim_all detaches the complete ordered chain, leaving domain head and tail null. maintenance and pending are set before unlock. Reentrant allocation/reset/trim/drain cannot reclaim the detached storage. It retains each metadata node until all callbacks finish and reconciliation locks again.

Rollback copies may contain previous/next values but are plain detached values, not linked objects. Only deallocate_backing or drop_claim consumes the local copy; neither reads or mutates previous/next. Backing destructor has no auto-unlink, provider callback or implicit claim removal. Uncertain retain/alias/deallocation paths continue charging and quarantine without replay.

Insertion order is preserved. Erase/detach/reset and pending publication keep prior invalidations. End remains a null iterator; successful pending publication invalidates cached end/lower bound before future use. No scan is replaced with weaker size/alignment assumptions.

8628 retains bounded scalar capacity prediction, explicit placement-new Record activation and lock-protected OPEN-notify elision from 9aca. Their earlier proof obligations were rechecked in the same source; this is not inheritance of any 9aca performance or validation result.

check_backing_list compares stable node identity and original payload against a separate vector order, both previous/next neighbors, begin/end, empty, front and last. Test covers fresh empty, empty/self whole-splice, eight appends, four head/middle/tail single transfers, endpoint erase, nonempty whole-splice, repeated middle erases through singleton, empty-target transfer and live nodes at destruction. Saved iterator is not read after its node is deleted. No scalar Backing allocation OOM injector is claimed.

primary_references.use: Conceptual intrusive links and explicit object lifetime, no imported implementation.
Avoid destructor unlinking that silently modifies shared list state.
Keep unlinking, metadata disposal and provider resource cleanup explicit.

material_costs_and_limits: Backing now contains two pointer links; actual Backing sizeof alone cannot be compared with the former list value without including former external list-node/header allocations.
Global RangeClaim registry remains std::list and its own allocations/scans remain. This change does not imply whole API zero allocation.
Fresh one-shot metadata-table growth remains, and capacity hints may amplify a later second-record request to128 slots.
No source-review claim proves a runtime speedup, allocator usable size, RSS, energy, device behavior or global algorithmic optimality.
This review starts no compiler, benchmark, test executable or device command. New candidate requires its own complete validation and performance round.
